scenario: A buyer is planning a twelve-month coffee-and-tea pantry for a remote location where replenishment is uncertain. Five exact frozen seller pages offer a three-bag whole-bean coffee, ground coffee in three steel cans, freeze-dried instant coffee in two resealable pouches, loose-leaf tea in two metal tins, and one hundred individually wrapped oolong tea bags. The corpus also contains concept pages about shelf life, vacuum packing, freeze drying, water activity, and rancidification, plus four individual community discussions about food-storage containers. It does not contain the exact lots' roast, pack, or best-before dates; package-film specifications; seal tests; measured water activity; the buyer's pantry temperature and humidity record; opened-package consumption duration; or a controlled twelve-month sensory comparison of the five exact products. The research problem is to decide what can be bought now, what must first be verified or trialed, how to size and rotate sealed units, and when to replenish or defer without converting seller packaging language or generic preservation mechanisms into a one-year freshness guarantee.

rules.seller_format_packaging_claim_boundary_v: The five frozen shopping pages establish exact seller-authored offers and packaging words. The whole-bean offer is three nominal 36-ounce bags at 39.95 dollars. The ground offer is three 12-ounce cans at 16.47 dollars and says canned for peak quality and that a steel can locks in aroma. The instant offer is two 7.05-ounce freeze-dried decaffeinated pouches at 40.98 dollars and says the Doypack bags are resealable and protect granules. The loose-leaf offer is two 100-gram metal tins at 24.99 dollars and says packed at source and garden fresh. The oolong offer is one hundred individually wrapped tea bags at 8.99 dollars. Those words, prices, ratings, review counts, formats, and package counts do not reveal the exact lot's dates, fill gas, residual oxygen, film or closure barrier, seal integrity, storage history, measured quality, or twelve-month outcome.
rules.shelf_life_condition_and_endpoint_specif: Shelf life is a recommended maximum period during which a defined quality for a specified proportion of goods remains acceptable under expected or specified distribution, storage, and display conditions. The concept page distinguishes pantry use, sale, best-before, use-by, freshness, safety, and quality, says a product past shelf life may remain safe while quality is no longer guaranteed, and identifies product-specific degradation plus light, heat, moisture, gas transmission, mechanical stress, and contamination. A duration is therefore inadmissible unless the exact endpoint, lot, unopened or opened state, package, temperature, humidity, light, handling, and decision threshold are declared.
rules.oxygen_moisture_heat_light_mechanism_bou: Vacuum packing can remove air before sealing and is intended to reduce oxygen, but its result depends on product, atmosphere, temperature, seal, and package barrier. Water activity describes equilibrium vapor behavior and can inform microbial and moisture-migration control, but it is not simply water concentration and requires product-specific measurement. Rancidification can arise from oxidation or hydrolysis under air, light, moisture, and related conditions and may produce undesirable odor and flavor. These mechanisms identify variables to measure; they do not authenticate any exact can, bag, pouch, tin, or wrapper, establish its residual oxygen or barrier, or assign a one-year sensory life.
rules.freeze_dried_instant_not_universal_senso: Freeze drying is a low-temperature dehydration process that freezes a product, lowers pressure, and removes ice by sublimation. The generic process can retain many original qualities after rehydration and is used for coffee and preservation. The Mount Hagen seller page additionally calls its exact product freeze dried and its two pouches resealable. Neither source establishes the exact lot's process control, water activity, package barrier, seal and reseal integrity, opened-pouch exposure, reconstituted sensory threshold, or twelve-month performance, so freeze-dried instant cannot be declared the universal winner without those checks.
rules.format_opening_and_lot_comparison_bounda: The three exact coffee offers differ simultaneously in product, roast and flavor copy, caffeine state, price, nominal quantity, format, package count, and seller. The corpus contains no matched trial isolating whole bean versus ground versus instant under the same lot age, package barrier, opening frequency, pantry conditions, preparation, and sensory endpoint. Compare them only after verifying exact lot dates and seals, converting quantity into servings, estimating time each independent unit remains open, and running a small controlled preparation and sensory calibration. Do not attribute a difference to format when product, lot, package, dose, or preparation also differs.
rules.tea_package_unitization_not_year_guarant: The loose-leaf page supports two 100-gram metal tins and seller language about packed at source and garden fresh. The oolong page supports one hundred individually wrapped tea bags. Multiple tins and individual wrappers may reduce how much product is exposed per opening, but the frozen pages do not specify wrapper or tin barrier, headspace, closure, seal integrity, pack date, best-before date, or sensory behavior after opening. Unitization must be converted into actual servings and open duration, then verified and trialed rather than treated as a twelve-month guarantee.
rules.community_container_scope_v1: The four community pages contain individual authors' container needs and uncontrolled replies about bent lids, leaks, stacking, glass breakage, freezer headspace, vacuum attachments, buckets, jars, and disputed airtightness. They can suggest inspection questions such as closure condition, stackability, odor, breakage, headspace, and whether an airtight claim is physically verified. They do not test the five exact coffee or tea products, their original packages, pantry conditions, microbial safety, sensory life, or a twelve-month rotation plan, and the replies cannot be treated as prevalence or comparative product evidence.
rules.staged_remote_pantry_trial_v1: Before a full-year commitment, obtain the shippable lot's roast or manufacture, pack, and best-before fields; photograph and inspect each independent seal and closure; record package material and any verified oxygen or moisture barrier data; log pantry temperature, relative humidity, light, pests, and handling; compute servings and expected days open per unit; and buy the smallest returnable or replaceable quantity. Use one preparation protocol and predeclared aroma, flavor, solubility, visible-moisture, odor, seal, and safety stop rules at opening and scheduled checkpoints. Stock only the number of sealed units that can remain within verified unopened and opened windows, rotate earliest dates first, keep a replenishment trigger, and defer any format whose critical fields or calibration fail.
rules.evidence_bounded_remote_pantry_rotation_: There is no corpus-supported universal winner among whole-bean bags, ground-coffee cans, freeze-dried instant pouches, loose-leaf tins, and individually wrapped tea bags. A format is admissible only if its exact lot dates, independent-unit count, package and seal fields, pantry conditions, serving schedule, opened duration, and predeclared quality and safety checkpoints are known and pass a small calibration. Among admissible configurations, choose the cheapest one that meets the buyer's taste, preparation, caffeine, quantity, and rotation constraints. Buy reserves in independent sealed units, open one unit at a time, use earliest verified dates first, replenish at the declared trigger, and defer or shorten the horizon when evidence remains missing.
